package.allocationCaveat: Both framework logical manifests and SHA-256 contents match. The before Electron Framework executable occupies 10,948,608 more allocated bytes despite equal size/content. Allocation varies independently of dependency pruning; logical whole-app byte savings are the causal package-size comparison.

findingStatus.details: Running Actions read status only. Final history is bounded to 1 MiB on the project host; capture failure cannot hide a known exit. Poll cadence and connection-wide Action batching remain unchanged.
Extracted byte-counted segmented replay; exact UTF-8 suffix and control bytes preserved within the existing 512 KiB bound.

Folder browsing, canonical directory verification, SSH project creation/LaTeX validation and connection tests are asynchronous. Notes/Actions metadata and several tmux lifecycle paths remain synchronous.
Worker-owned archive catalog, incremental parsing, and bounded transcript cache remain next-stage work.
Canonical-location queue protects comment migration/create/delete across service instances in one process. Separate clients/processes and alternate SSH aliases still need host-side conflict handling.

Shared three-read gate across previews/generations; 16 unique project-image paths and 16 MiB accepted data-URL text per document. Duplicate DOM copies also count. Queued reads cancel; already issued IPC retains its slot until settlement. Viewport admission and external HTTPS image budgeting remain outside this change.
Immutable PDF snapshot ownership and bounded hot storage require preserving exact displayed/printed snapshots.
Monaco model ownership and dirty-draft protection need a shared registry with split-pane ownership before cache eviction changes.
Moved 13 renderer-only libraries to build dependencies without version changes. Preserved runtime dependencies, native helpers and renderer license/notice files.
Inactive terminal workspaces no longer append an uncached fallback tab. Actual xterm surface count stays within the physical pane four-entry LRU.
Visibility-aware Git/document scheduling and explicit background auto-compile policy remain separate work.
Concurrent reconnect/discovery reads share one in-flight scan per connection. Per-session backoff remains; staggered requests can still create separate scans.
Demand-driven headless parsing and parser/IPC backpressure need dedicated high-output stress tests.
Archive catalog reuse, remote history pagination and cache ownership remain separate work.
PDF page acquisition remains eager; all 500 pages are still requested in the control workload.
Clean document asset budgets and revision-cached annotation anchoring remain separate work.
Hidden LaTeX chats explicitly suppress terminal input/resize and composer sends while preserving chat, draft and backend.
Legacy duplicate-output migration requires exact-byte migration/reopen tests; no database migration was added here.
Ordered startup migrations and newer-schema refusal remain separate work.
All five Drive existence/context lookups use runtime project snapshots without replay hydration. Activity/editorial history pagination and Git count caching remain unchanged.
Durable-output batching is unchanged; WAL benchmark remains a control, not a claimed improvement.

limitations: No calibrated watts, battery life, wakeup, real network throughput or full-application speedup measured.
Replay timing covers retention only, excluding PTY, parsers, IPC and renderer. Other host applications were not stopped.
Markdown byte budget describes accepted data-URL text; concurrent response payloads and browser decoding can require extra transient memory. HTTPS images retain existing browser loading.
Synthetic IPC tests do not establish behavior of every real server or provider.
Packages are unsigned isolated validation artifacts. No installed app or release was updated.
